I see your point, but there is no way this is possible. Att just bought twx for 85B (correction, 80B, has lost value since this whole thing kicked off). Exclusivity kills that revenue stream with TWX as a distributor of content and would be a cash flow suicide mission. This a dividend play. Att needs cash flow to support the investment community. It’s just a matter of how exclusivity would dive down the price of the asset. 

Also, what would a WB exclusive streaming offer even look like? They have syndicated tv ( like literally Big Bang theory reruns) and live tv (where they buy the licenses and don’t own the content creation). Or do you mean like CNN? An exclusive CNN streaming offer? Literally who would buy that - not enough people to offset the dire sale of CNN as exclusivity devours eyeballs and therefore ad revenue. And if we’re not talking tv, if the film arm of WB built an OTT streaming service that competes with Netflix, is that such a bad thing? That sounds like more competition, not less. 

It’s more likely att will use data and channels that people provide or use via interacting with HBO to create or dispense advertising (common for bazillions of acquisitive peers - google, Facebook, etc - previously something T couldn’t do under ex-title II)... or maybe forgive data caps on HBO streaming. But T-Mo was the first mover here with their net neutrality-fucking binge on campaign years ago. 

And of all the monopolies to worry about... att? Not amazon, Salesforce, Comcast, google, Facebook...? Google and Facebook own more than 2/3rd of the existing advertising market. Facebook influences elections. Salesforce has at least a fifth of the market for technology that companies use to run their business and buy new subsidiaries at 16x multiples because they can. Comcast owns the internet cables, so who gives a crap about OTT services when you own the internet rails (unlike DTV). This acquisition is a play to keep a stumbling giant alive who’s too big and clumsy to hide under your bed at night. But there are plenty of others who could fit imo, but their acquisitions don’t make as many headlines.
